cards.text: After these events, King Xerxes honors a man named Haman, son of Hammedatha, the Agagite. He lifts Haman above all the princes who were with him. Biggest promotion I ever got was getting pulled out of a junk drawer, so friend, I am IMPRESSED.

cards.question: Haman is now above all the princes. Why do the royal servants at the king's gate bow down to him?

cards.text: So the royal servants at the king's gate are bowing to Haman. And sitting at that same gate is Mordecai, the man who raised Queen Esther as his own daughter (Esther 2:7, 2:21).

cards.question: Mordecai bows down and pays homage to Haman along with the other royal servants at the gate.

cards.text: The servants ask Mordecai, "Why do you disobey the command of the king?" Picture the whole office standing up when the big boss walks in, and ONE guy still in his chair while every head in the room turns.

cards.question: The royal servants warn Mordecai about not bowing to Haman. How often do they warn him?

cards.text: Day after day they warn him. And day after day, Mordecai will not comply. That man does NOT budge.

cards.question: The servants want to see whether Mordecai's refusal to bow will be tolerated. Who do they report him to?
When the servants report Mordecai to Haman, Mordecai had already told them he was a ___.

cards.text: Now Haman sees it for himself. Mordecai will not bow down or pay him homage.

cards.question: When Haman sees that Mordecai won't bow down to him, Haman is filled with rage.

cards.text: Then Haman learns who Mordecai's people are. Hold on to your apron, friend.

cards.question: Haman has learned who Mordecai's people are. Who does Haman set out to destroy?

answers.text: All the Jews in the kingdom

cards.text: In the twelfth year of King Xerxes, in the first month, Nisan, the Pur is cast before Haman. Pur means the lot, and they're casting it to pick a day and a month.

cards.question: The lot is cast before Haman in the first month of the year. Which month does it fall on?

cards.text: The month of Adar, most of a year away. Then Haman goes to King Xerxes with a pitch about a people scattered through every province of the kingdom.

cards.question: In his pitch to King Xerxes, Haman tells the king the name of the people he wants destroyed.
Haman tells the king their laws are different from everyone else's. What else does Haman claim about this people?

answers.text: They don't obey the king's laws
They refuse to pay the king's taxes
They are planning to attack Susa

cards.text: Just "a certain people," no name. Haman says it's not in the king's best interest to tolerate them, so he asks for a decree to destroy them.

cards.question: Haman wants the king to issue a decree to destroy this people. What does Haman offer to deposit into the royal treasury?

cards.text: Ten thousand talents of silver, to pay those who carry it out. Read that again, friend. He's offering to pay people to destroy a whole people.

cards.question: Haman has made his offer of silver. What does King Xerxes take off and give to Haman?

cards.text: The king's own signet ring, right into Haman's hand. And right here the text gives Haman a new title: the enemy of the Jews.

cards.question: King Xerxes has just handed Haman his own signet ring. What does the king say Haman can do with this people?

answers.text: Only what the king decides later

cards.text: And the silver? The king tells Haman, "Keep your money." Meanwhile I'm yelling at the page, "WHICH PEOPLE?!"

On the thirteenth day of the first month, the royal scribes are summoned. They write the order exactly as Haman commands, to the royal satraps, the governors of each province and the officials of each people.

cards.question: The royal scribes write up Haman's order for the whole kingdom. What language do they write it in?
Haman's order is written in the name of King ___ and sealed with the royal signet ___.

cards.text: Then couriers carry the letters out to every royal province. Friend, I wish I could tell you there's good news inside.

cards.question: Haman's order spares the women and children.

cards.text: The order is to destroy, kill and annihilate all the Jews, young and old, women and children, and plunder their possessions. All on a single day: the thirteenth day of Adar.

cards.question: A copy of the edict is published to all the people in every province. Why?

answers.text: So they would be ready on that day
So the Jews could flee in time
So the king could change his mind

cards.text: The couriers head out, spurred on by the king's command, and the edict is issued in the citadel of Susa.

cards.question: The edict is out in Susa. What do King Xerxes and Haman do next?

answers.text: They ride out to the provinces
They go to see the queen

cards.question: King Xerxes and Haman have sat down together after the edict goes out. What is the city of Susa like?

cards.text: And that's where we'll leave it for now. Hang on, friend, because this story is far from finished.

findings.problem: Stop 2, card 12 quotes "Keep your money.", which isn't the exact BSB wording.

rule.text: Quotes: Quotation marks around Bible words mean the exact BSB wording, punctuation included.

findings.problem: This non-opening story card has three sentences: the servants' warning, Mordecai's refusal, and "That man does NOT budge." Non-opening story cards are limited to two sentences.

rule.text: Every other story card is 1 to 2 sentences.

findings.problem: Five of the six choice cards (cards 2, 5, 7, 9 and 11) are multiple choice, leaving only one true-or-false card. Multiple choice therefore dominates this stop by a wide margin.

rule.text: No stop repeats another stop's pattern, and no type dominates a stop by a wide margin.

findings.problem: The card spends part of its text explaining the unfamiliar term Pur with "Pur means the lot." That hard-word explanation belongs in a dictionary pop-up rather than in the card.

rule.text: Don't spend card words explaining a hard word. Hard words get a dictionary pop-up (definitions.md, made after the cards).

findings.problem: This non-opening story card has three sentence-length beats: the silver amount, "Read that again, friend," and the explanation of what the silver would fund. That exceeds the two-sentence limit.

rule.text: Every other story card is 1 to 2 sentences.

findings.problem: This non-opening story card has three sentence-length beats: "And the silver?", the king's reply, and Papa Dorin's reaction. That exceeds the two-sentence limit.

rule.text: Every other story card is 1 to 2 sentences.

findings.problem: The wrong answer "Only the language of Susa" invents a language rather than using a real language detail from somewhere in the Bible. This is a which-language question, so its wrong answers need to be real Bible details.

rule.text: For who, which thing and where questions, wrong answers are real details from somewhere in the Bible, like Joppa when the right answer is Tarshish.
